145.81104,-35.01417.name: DIR 203 — Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.) field trial (site 11), Murrumbidgee Council
145.81104,-35.01417.type: Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.), licensed field trial
145.81104,-35.01417.desc: WHAT. A licensed GMO crop field trial site, Herbicide tolerance and insect resistance, held by Monsanto Australia Pty Ltd. WHERE IT SITS. OGTR named the council area this site is in and published no coordinate on the page this was read from, so this marker sits in that council area and not at the trial itself. WHY IT MATTERS. OGTR names the council area of every licensed site, its area in hectares and the licence it runs under. No other register on this map states where a release is at all, which is the comparison worth making even at this resolution.

-87.92870,41.80010.name: RUSH Center for Advanced Reproductive Care
-87.92870,41.80010.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: John S. Rinehart, MD, PHD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

139.49093,35.33886.name: Shonan Health Innovation Park
139.49093,35.33886.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of iPark Institute Co., Ltd.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.13907,51.56648.name: Fertility Centre at Whittington Health
-0.13907,51.56648.state: Clinic 4C, Whittington Hospital, Magdala Avenue, London, N19 5NF
-0.13907,51.56648.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-46.65841,-23.55012.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: www.ceerh.com.br. -117.21960,32.87600.name: Illumina
-117.21960,32.87600.desc: Illumina has dominated DNA sequencing for over a decade, and the cost curve it drove is why reading a genome went from a national project to a line item. Almost every genome on this map — prenatal screens, newborn programmes, embryo screening, pathogen surveillance, consumer ancestry tests, crop breeding — was read on its machines or a competitor built in response to them. That position is closer to a monopoly than anything else here, and it is held through instruments plus the consumable reagents each run requires, which is where the revenue is. Regulators in the US and EU blocked its acquisition of the cancer-test maker Grail on the grounds that owning both the sequencers and a test that runs on them would let it disadvantage every rival test; it completed the deal anyway, was fined, and divested in 2024. It is the clearest case on this map of a company whose product is not an organism but without which most of the rest could not operate.

83.12000,54.92000.name: Vector State Research Centre of Virology and Biotechnology
83.12000,54.92000.desc: One of two facilities in the world authorised to hold live smallpox, the other being the US CDC. It has had a documented explosion and a laboratory-acquired infection. Whether the remaining stocks should be destroyed has been argued at the World Health Assembly for decades and repeatedly deferred — and since the sequence is published, the argument is now partly moot.

-63.18210,-17.78330.name: ANAPO — Asociación de Productores de Oleaginosas y Trigo
-63.18210,-17.78330.desc: Bolivia authorised herbicide-tolerant soy by decree in 2005 and drought-tolerant HB4 soy in March 2026, the second announced at Exposoya, a trade fair ANAPO itself organises. The minister who made the announcement had been ANAPO's president for two terms immediately before taking office. Roughly nine tenths of Bolivian soy is engineered and the great majority of it grows in Santa Cruz. This is the clearest case on the map of the applicant, the trade body and the approving ministry being the same small circle of people, and it is documented in the government's own announcement rather than alleged.

-0.18700,5.60400.name: Genome editing guidelines — Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya and Malawi
-0.18700,5.60400.desc: Ghana's National Biosafety Authority published Guidelines on Genome Editing on 30 October 2023, setting out which categories of genome-edited organisms and products are regulated under the Biosafety Act 2011 (Act 831) — making it the fourth African country with validated genome-editing guidelines, after Nigeria, Kenya and Malawi. Four of the countries whose biosafety authorities this map already records have therefore drawn the same line as Argentina, and none of those records mentioned it. Note what the instrument is in each case: guidelines issued by the biosafety authority under an existing biosafety act, rather than an exemption from it — the regulator keeps the decision about what falls inside its own statute.
